title: Scheduler fuzz testbed — observations and action items
summary: Working notes from a parameter-space fuzzing testbed for the continuous batching scheduler. Goal: characterize brittle corners where small changes in timeout/batch-size/fairness produce large jumps in p95/p99 and fairness regressions across priority classes.
motivation_and_goal: We keep hitting intermittent tail spikes in production traces that are not reproduced by our deterministic sweep harness. Hypothesis: non-linear interactions between flush timeouts, max batch windows, and demotion thresholds cause stateful oscillations. The fuzz testbed mutates multiple knobs stochastically while replaying realistic traces to surface worst-case pockets and modes.
testbed_setup_and_controls:
- Harness: dockerized runner (cpu/gpu job) that replays trace files with request timing fidelity and injects microbursts.
- Scheduler under test: local build from main w/ debug hooks enabled (latency tracing, occupancy histograms, per-slot age stats).
- Metric sinks: Prometheus-style push gateway + per-run trace dumps (ndjson events).
- Profiling: perf + nvprof sampling on problematic runs; flamegraphs captured for CPU hot paths.
- Isolation: single-node GPU (A100 equivalent), pinned cores for the scheduler thread to reduce noise.
traffic_traces_used:
- real-prod-2024-06-peerchat-sampled.json (diurnal + microburst windows)
- synthetic-microburst-10kspike-200ms.json (short heavy bursts)
- steady-300rps-long-tail.json (long tails simulated)
Notes: We randomized seed across replay to avoid alignment artifacts.
parameter_space_explored:
Ranges (fuzzed):
- max_batch_size: 8..512
- flush_timeout_ms: 1..200
- age_based_demote_ms: 2..150
- fairness_weight_high: 0.1..5.0
- preemption_cutoff: 0..0.9 (fraction of batch)
- slot_count: 1..16
We performed ~1.2k stochastic runs combining random draws of the above plus 20 controlled grid sweeps for corner cases.
observability_signals_collected:
- p50/p95/p99/p999 latencies (end-to-end)
- per-request queue time, execution time, kv-cache hit flag
- batch size distribution per flush
- slot occupancy over time
- per-priority class throughput and latency (high/normal/low)
- scheduler walltime breakdown: selection, assembly, enqueue, flush
- allocation stalls (GPU context switch counters)
key_findings_summary:
1) Non-monotonic p99 vs flush_timeout: there is a mid-range timeout (~15–45ms) where p99 spikes dramatically for mixed-traffic traces. Very low timeout (<5ms) keeps tail low but hurts throughput; very high timeout (>120ms) increases latency but reduces tail variability.
2) Fairness oscillation mode: when fairness_weight_high > 2.2 and preemption_cutoff is low, high-priority flows hog slots and then demote, creating alternating windows of starvation for normal traffic — p99 doubles periodically.
3) Batch-size instability: allowing max_batch_size > 256 together with an aggressive age_demote cutoff caused occasional "mode collapse" where the scheduler coalesces massively during bursts then flushes giant batches creating GPU saturation spikes and queueing after flush lasting hundreds of ms.
4) KV cache interaction: certain parameter combos increase KV-cache miss rate because older queries are more likely to be collated into batches with different contexts; miss penalties correlate with p999 events.
5) Slot_count effect: fewer slots (1–2) amplify contention; with >8 slots we see improved isolation but more variance in batch sizes across slots which hurts tail in mixed-priority traces.
notable_runs_and_anomalies:
- Run #427 (trace: real-prod-2024-06) random seed 9834: flush_timeout_ms=28, max_batch_size=384, fairness_weight_high=3.0 -> saw p99 jump from 78ms baseline to 420ms. Flamegraph: high CPU time in slot-selection loop due to repeated eviction churn.
- Run #901 (synthetic-microburst) seed 2101: preemption_cutoff=0.05 caused rapid demotion thrashing; observed oscillation period ~400ms. nvprof showed GPU kernel queueing peaks coincident with large batch flushes.
- Run #1123 (steady 300rps) seed 4491: very low timeout (2ms) maintained tail but throughput dropped 18% and GPU utilization fell from 76% -> 62%.
profiling_notes:
- CPU hotspots: batch-assembly hot loop (lock contention on slot metadata), and a small memcpy path that scales poorly for large batch sizes.
- NVidia metrics: kernel launch latency increases when many small kernels are launched in close succession; large batches amortize launch overhead but cause longer single-kernel durations leading to head-of-queue blocking.
- Suggestion: add per-slot lightweight sampling to detect eviction churn early and throttle assemble rate.
actionable_recommendations:
- Safe defaults: max_batch_size=128, flush_timeout_ms=12, age_demote_ms=20, fairness_weight_high=1.0, preemption_cutoff=0.25, slot_count=4. These provide a balanced tradeoff across traces in our tests.
- Add a chaos monitor that detects oscillatory fairness patterns (periodic p99 spikes across classes) and triggers a temporary fallback to conservative fairness settings.
- Implement an async assembly path for very large batches to reduce lock contention on scheduler thread.
- Instrument kv-cache hit flags at batch granularity and emit warning when aggregated per-batch miss rate > 0.15.
- Add a targeted guard that limits batch growth when GPU kernel queue length exceeds a threshold (protect downstream latency).
open_questions_and_followups:
- Why do certain mid-range timeouts produce worse tails than larger timeouts? Need microtrace correlation between queue growth and KV-cache behavior.
- Can we design a lightweight admission-control filter that drops coalescing for requests labeled as latency-sensitive (by API flag)?
- Run testbed across a heterogeneous multi-GPU node (mixed A100+V100) to validate kernel scheduling assumptions.
- Evaluate adding small randomized jitter to flush_timeout to break pathological alignment.

appendix_quick-runbook:
How to reproduce a run locally:
1) ./dev/run_fuzz_harness --trace real-prod-2024-06.json --seed 9834 --max-runs 1 --out /tmp/fuzz
2) export SCHED_DEBUG=1 && ./bazel-bin/serving/runtime --config debug.yaml
3) ./tools/collect-trace /tmp/fuzz > /tmp/fuzz.ndjson
4) ./tools/visualize-latency /tmp/fuzz.ndjson
Notes: add --pin-scheduler-core to reduce jitter.
